title: 3952. Maximum Total Value of Covered Indices

examples.explanation: Initially, indices 1 and 3 contain tokens. Move the token from index 3 to index 2. Move the token from index 1 to index 0. The covered indices are [0, 2], so the total value is nums[0] + nums[2] = 9 + 6 = 15.
Initially, only index 2 contains a token. It is optimal to leave the token at index 2. The covered index is [2], so the total value is nums[2] = 4.
Initially, indices 1 and 2 contain tokens. Move the token from index 1 to index 0. The covered indices are [0, 2], so the total value is nums[0] + nums[2] = 9 + 5 = 14.

hints: 1a (Greedy). Consider each maximal block of consecutive tokens independently, together with the index immediately before the block if it exists.
1b (Greedy). From this range, every index except one can be covered, so subtract the minimum nums value in the range.
2a (DP). A token at index i can only end at i or i - 1.
2b (DP). Process indices from left to right and keep whether the previous index is already covered; try both choices for the current token when possible.
